text:
Maya: Noticing strange billing blips in the last hour correlated with streaming resume events. Routes that had failovers show a short window where sessions are double-counted. Console shows ~600 active_sessions, billing pipeline shows ~900 for the same route for ~3m.

Ravi: Which route/region? Any recent rollout that touched resume logic or sticky routing?

Maya: us-central, traffic spiked after the region drain earlier. We rolled a small sticky-routing tweak last night but that was at midnight. This looks like a mid-flight route-swap during resume.

Em: Could be resume-token namespace collision when the session is migrated between shards. If the resume token is reissued while the old connection hasn't fully tombstoned, both sides count active.

Kai: Do we have logs showing resume accept vs old session closure? Sample from proxy: 
```
[2026-04-01T14:02:13Z] resume_request token=tok-xyz route=us-central shard=sh-12
[2026-04-01T14:02:13Z] resume_accepted session_id=sess-888 -> sess-889
[2026-04-01T14:02:14Z] old_session_closed session_id=sess-888 reason=peer_reset
```
Note the accepted event precedes closure by ~1s. That could be due to async route-handoff.

Ravi: That ordering would cause metrics to briefly record two active sessions. But our counters should be idempotent based on token. What metric key are we using? session_id or resume_token?

Maya: Console uses session_id dedupe, billing uses resume_token dedupe (older pipeline). When the resume creates a new session_id before the old one decrements, the two systems disagree.

Em: Hmm. Two independent dedupe keys -> race. We need a unified canonical identity for counting, ideally resume_token when present, fallback to session_id if token missing. But changing billing pipeline is risky.

Kai: Telemetry ingestion lag compounds this: console aggregates in near-real-time (~10s), billing pipeline ingests with ~45s latency. If the resume ordering flips between pipelines, the transient difference appears longer.

metrics-bot: Alert: us-central resume_dup_rate > 0.8% for 5m. Threshold 0.5%.

Maya: Proposed short-term mitigations: 1) Add a tiny grace TTL on the console side where session_id counts remain suppressed for 2s after a new session_id with same resume_token appears. 2) Add an out-of-band event `resume_in_progress` that both console and billing can subscribe to (shadow) so they align.

Ravi: 2s grace feels arbitrary. What if networks are slower? We should make TTL adaptive: base on observed median handoff latency per route (p50) + safety margin. For us-central p50 is ~120ms so 2s seems safe, but make it configurable.

Em: Agree on adaptive TTL. Also we should avoid adding new cardinal labels to billing metrics. For console it's fine. For billing, do shadow computation using resume_token -> canonical_count and compare for a week before switch.

Kai: Could we instead change the resume code path to try to close the old session synchronously before acknowledging the resume? That reduces races but risks adding latency to resume path which clients might notice. Might be acceptable for short windows.

Maya: Good point. We can gate that behavior behind a feature flag and enable it for canary routes only. Implementation: attempt sync close with a 500ms deadline; if it times out, fall back to async handoff.

Ravi: Concern: synchronous close could create a tail latency spike for streaming reconnects. Let's limit canary to internal traffic first. Also add metrics: `resume.sync_close_duration_ms` and `resume.sync_close_failed` to monitor.

Em: On the console side I'll add UI hints: when resume events are detected show a small banner "Resume activity detected: counts may be transiently inflated" with a link to diagnostic panel that shows resume_token mapping and real-time reconciliation.

metrics-bot: Info: created temporary dashboard panel `resume-token-map` sampling 5% of events.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-1401 opened for us-central resume duplication spike.

Kai: Operational checklist: - implement adaptive grace TTL in console aggregator - instrument resume_token in edge logs (sampled) - add `resume_in_progress` event to event bus - shadow dedupe in billing pipeline - feature flag for sync-close attempt - dashboard panel + alert tweaks.

Maya: I'll own the console aggregator change + banner UX. Will add tests that simulate out-of-order events.

Ravi: I'll own the proxy change: sampled resume_token emit + sync-close feature flag. I'll prepare a canary plan: 1% internal -> 5% internal -> 10% internal -> evaluate for 24h -> consider customer canary.

Em: I'll do the billing shadow run and generate delta reports. Finance will want a CSV of delta by customer for the 24h window. I'll schedule that.

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: edge-proxy/feat/resume-sync-close @ 2026-04-01T18:00:00Z (internal canary 1%).

Maya: Can someone add a quick Kibana saved search for `resume_accepted` events with latency histogram? That will be useful during canary.

Kai: On it, creating `kibana: ResumeHandoffLatency` in the us-central space.

Ravi: One more thought: update runbooks to instruct on-call to check both `active_sessions` and `resume_dup_rate` before paging. If dup rate < 0.2% ignore; else escalate.

Maya: I'll update the streaming runbook and add the new thresholds.

Em: OK let's proceed with the plan. If anyone sees the billing delta > 5% in the canary bucket, hold rollout and roll back the sync-close flag.

Maya: PRs incoming: console aggregator + banner. Will link once ready.

Ravi: Starting proxy change now. Will post canary IDs and deploy time.

Maya: Thanks all.
